Two consortia submit bids, says report

Majda Muhsen ,  ZAWYA Projects

Kuwait Authority for Partnership Projects (KAPP) has opened technical bids for the 500-megawatt (MW) Al Dibdibah Power and Al Shagaya Renewable Energy Phase III – Zone 2 project, located within the Shagaya Renewable Energy Park (SREP) in Jahra Governorate, according to a report by local daily Al-Rai on Monday.

The report said two consortiums submitted technical proposals for the solar power project. The Higher Committee for PPP Projects is expected to proceed with the evaluation process before opening the financial bids and selecting a preferred bidder, it added.

No details were disclosed regarding the identities of the two consortia, or the timeline for opening financial bids.

In October 2025, KAPP, the Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy, and the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR) prequalified nine bidders and consortiums to compete for the project.

The prequalified entities included:

·       Consortium led by Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power with Kuwait's Alternative Energy Projects Company (AEPC Energy)

·       Consortium led by France's EDF Renewables with Kuwait's Abdullah Al Hamad Al Sagar & Brothers and South Korea's Korean Western Power

·       Consortium led by China's Jinko Power HK with Kuwait's Combined Group Contracting Company (CGC)

·       Consortium led by UAE-based Masdar with Kuwait's Fouad Alghanim & Sons General Trading & Contracting Company

·       Consortium led by US-based Swift Current Energy (SCE) with Kuwait's Arizona National for General Trading & Contracting Company

·       France's TotalEnergies Renewables

·       Turkey's Limak Yatirim Enerji Uretim Isletme Hizmetleri ve Insaat

·       Turkey's Kalyon Enerji Yatirimlari

·       Consortium led by China's Tianjin Zhonghuan New Energy, alongside Sinotec and Kuwait's Mohammed Abdulmohsin Al-Kharafi & Sons

The project will be backed by a 30-year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the offtaker Ministry of Electricity, Water, and Renewable Energy.

(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
